target.route: Original 3DS content; separate P3-side and P4-side clear archives

areas.name: Dual-Screen Route Archive
areas.location_cue: The file-creation screen and the school hub before committing to a labyrinth.
areas.note: This area contains route and save preparation only; it reveals no later plot.

save_backup.title: Keep a protected manual branch
save_backup.why: Create separate permanent files before choosing either protagonist perspective.
save_backup.detail: Retain the preceding file until every record in this area is checked.

point_of_no_return.title: Archive this state before advancing

levels.1: Use the only official version.
levels.2: Use a legally dumped 3DS copy with a readable dual-screen layout.
levels.3: Run the original Nintendo 3DS release on owned hardware or a successor-compatible 3DS emulator. Keep the lower map screen large enough to draw accurately, raise internal resolution only for the upper view, and record emulator build plus region before starting.

levels.1: One opening choice changes the viewpoint.
levels.2: Create an independent file for the P3-side perspective.
levels.3: Start a fresh file with the P3-side protagonist, keep its manual saves separate, finish the route, and preserve the resulting clear data. Do not overwrite it when beginning the other perspective because a later optional battle checks both route clears.

levels.1: The other viewpoint needs its own record.
levels.2: Create an independent file for the P4-side perspective.
levels.3: Start a fresh file with the P4-side protagonist, use a separate save tree, finish that perspective, and retain its clear data alongside the P3-side archive. Route-specific conversations and several request answers differ even though dungeon geometry is shared.

levels.1: Choose the locked difficulty only on a prepared file.
levels.2: Risky must be selected when the file is created.
levels.3: Select Risky at new-file creation and treat the choice as permanent. Keep the protagonist protected because their defeat ends the attempt, and carry Sutakora Foot for forced FOE contact because the ordinary escape command is unavailable there.

levels.1: Protect route, request, floor, and clear states.
levels.2: Reserve separate slots for route choice, timed requests, current floor, and clear data.
levels.3: Maintain four rotating records: the untouched route file, a save before the current progression gate, a floor-entry save, and the latest safe hub return. Add permanent clear-data slots for both protagonist perspectives rather than recycling them.

levels.1: The lower-screen map has its own recovery value.
levels.2: Save drawn map data whenever a failed expedition added useful tiles.
levels.3: After a defeat, preserve newly drawn map information when the game offers that choice, then reload the combat state. Verify the floor percentage and annotations before continuing; clear data can carry those maps into the second route.

levels.1: Check what the second file inherits.
levels.2: Carry maps, registry, money, items, and party levels into the next cycle.
levels.3: Load clear data and explicitly choose the carryover set. Confirm map percentages, Compendium registration, currency, non-key inventory, and party levels before leaving the hub; main Personas transfer, while equipped Sub-Personas must be rebuilt from the registry.
